publication.title: Desperately Searching for Travel Offers? Formulate Better Queries with Some Help from Linked Data

source_reading.scope: Abstract, semantic graph/model and verbalization (§§3.1–3.3), query assistance (§3.4), experiment setup and discussion (§4), conclusion (§5).

adjudication.basis: RE-ONE implements interactive criteria discovery and refinement supported by a typed semantic destination graph, with suggestions constrained to remaining travel offers. It supplies a counterbalanced user comparison. Scope is KG-assisted search rather than direct node-link browsing.

codes.notes: RE-ONE controlled semantic criteria and content-aware follow-up suggestions; destination RDF transformed to offer indexes. No underlying query language inferred. Longer/richer queries do not prove booking success.

report_level_evaluation.design: 34 French speakers aged 23–35, divided equally into short-trip and long-trip scenarios; each uses RE-ONE and Google Custom Search on the same catalogue, with order counterbalanced.
report_level_evaluation.measures: Words per query; Criteria per query; Self-reported provenance of criteria
report_level_evaluation.results: Not reported; limits: Longer/richer queries and accepted suggestions do not directly establish booking satisfaction or task-completion superiority. Three reviewers are not user participants; the two scenarios are not 68 independent users. Controlled vocabulary shapes the provenance comparison.
